thread:
rachel: heads-up: customer Pelagos delivered a LoRA (v1.0). I merged into `cust/pelagos/lora-merged` and QA reports subtle list/numbering glitches and an extra trailing space on short responses. Blocking onboarding sign-off.

imran: can you paste a tiny repro from the smoke suite?

rachel: sure — minimal example:
```
Prompt: "Give the three main risks for the deployment."
Expected: "1) Network instability
2) Model drift
3) Insufficient monitoring"
Merged: "1) Network instability\n2) Model drift\n3) Insufficient monitoring \"  <-- extra trailing space/token
```

pavel: trailing-space + numbering shift often equals special-token or tokenizer ordering mismatch. Did Pelagos include tokenizer metadata?

rachel: they included `meta.json` with `"tokenizer": "spm_unigram"` and a small `vocab_map.txt`. Our runtime is `redwood-b2-bpe`. I ran our remap tool but still see fringe diffs.

sasha: quick check: run tokenized-seq-diff across the smoke pack before/after merge. We should gate merges on that metric.

rachel: ran `scripts/seq_diff.py --base-model redwood/b2 --lora artifacts/pelagos/lora-v1 --prompts evals/pelagos_smoke_180.json` and got `token_shift_ratio=0.0075` (0.75%).

imran: our current soft gate is 1.0% but for formatting-sensitive customers we use 0.5%. Pelagos wants tight formatting so treat as sensitive.

pavel: add a remap for special tokens explicitly — default remap sometimes leaves EOS/BOS order different which yields trailing whitespace/newline tokens. Use `tools/remap_specials.py --from spm_unigram --to redwood-b2` and verify special order.

rachel: did that: token_shift_ratio dropped to 0.003 (0.3%). Much better.

sasha: good. Now about quantization: did you test fp16 vs int8 vs int4? Past customer merges show int4 amplifies these subtle token shifts into larger hallucination diffs.

rachel: kicked off a quick eval pack (150 prompts) to compare quant levels. Command used:
```
./bin/run_quick_eval \
  --model artifacts/pelagos/lora-merged \
  --quant fp16,int8,int4 \
  --prompts evals/pelagos_smoke_150.json \
  --out /tmp/pelagos_eval_summary.json
```

eval-bot: quick-eval submitted job=44557 logs=https://ci.redwood/jobs/44557/logs

imran: FYI our int4 kernel on the N2 nodes has a known fused-op reorder sensitivity; int8 tends to match fp16 behavior closer for tokenizer-bound regressions. Default to int8 for new customer artifacts until we validate int4.

rachel: preliminary numbers from job artifacts: fp16 acc 0.73, int8 0.71, int4 0.62. Most regressions were punctuation/listing and short-table formatting. Attached top diffs in artifacts.

pavel: plan proposal: 1) require explicit special-token remap when metadata.tokenizer != model.tokenizer; 2) add `check_token_shift.py` as a pre-merge CI hook that computes token_shift_ratio and fails if >0.5% for `customer_sensitive=true`; 3) default new LoRA artifacts to int8 in Dedicated/Private until int4 kernel validation passes; 4) add SE-facing checklist requesting original tokenizer model or a token-map from customers.

sasha: +1. Also suggest CI warning band 0.2%-0.5% open a triage task instead of auto-fail so product/SE can review.

rachel: I'll open a PR with the remap helper, the CI hook, and an onboarding doc snippet. Will re-run the int8 quick eval after PR merge and post links here. ETA: EOD local time.

imran: one more thing — add a unit test to the merge pipeline that verifies special-token order invariants after remap (BOS/EOS/PAD/UNK) to catch regressions automatically.

pavel: agreed. I'll add that test in the PR.

sasha: thanks — ping here with PR and final eval results. :thumbsup:
